# Onboarding

## Use when
- A new user or new workspace needs a few answers before the product is useful (use case, name, invite teammates).
- Features need guided first use after setup: a checklist of 3 to 7 tasks with progress.

## Don't use when
- The user only signs in or verifies a code. That is the Auth pattern.
- Collecting many unrelated details up front. Ask only what changes the first screen; collect the rest in context later.
- Explaining a single new feature to existing users. Use a `Toast` or an inline `Alert variant="info"`, not a flow.

## Decision rules
- Two stages. Stage 1 is a short blocking setup flow of 3 to 5 steps, one question per step. Stage 2 is a non-blocking "Get started" checklist on the home screen. Why: Linear and Vercel use a short setup, then a checklist; Notion and Perplexity add a use-case question first.
- One primary `Button` per step ("Continue"). Back is `Button variant="ghost"` and always available except on step 1. Show progress as labelled steps (`Progress` with `label` and `valueLabel`, for example "Step 2 of 4"). Why: Wise labels its steps; Linear and Perplexity use dots.
- A choice between 2 to 4 named paths ("For my team", "Personal", "School") → `RadioGroup variant="card"`, each item with `label` and a one-line `description`. Selecting a card does not advance; Continue does. Why: Notion, Perplexity and Vercel plan type.
- Free-text answers → `Label` + `Input`. Role or company size → `Select`. Never ask for something the product can infer.
- Every optional step has a visible "Skip" (`Button variant="ghost"`) or "I'll do this later" on invite steps. Skipping must not trap the user in a half-set-up state. Why: Linear "I'll do this later".
- Checklist: a `Card variant="outlined"` titled "Get started" with a `Progress` ("3 of 6 complete"). Each row is a `ListItem` with title, one line of why, and an action; done rows show a check and strike through. The checklist can be dismissed and comes back from a menu. Why: Vercel Production Checklist, Klaviyo and HoneyBook setup guides, Dropbox "Get to know".
- Completion: replace the checklist with one confirmation line and one primary action ("Go to home"), not a full-screen celebration. Why: Klaviyo "Set up complete".
- Save answers as the user moves. Leaving and returning resumes at the same step.
- A failed save → one `Alert variant="danger"` above Continue; keep the answers. See the Error recovery pattern.

## Components and variants
- `Progress`
- `RadioGroup` variant: `card` · size: `md`
- `Label` variant: `default` · size: `md`
- `Input` variant: `default` · size: `md`
- `Select` size: `md`
- `Button` variant: `primary`, `ghost` · size: `md`
- `Card` variant: `outlined` · size: `md`
- `ListItem` variant: `outline` · size: `md`
- `Alert` variant: `danger` · size: `md`

## Layout and density
- Setup flow: one centred column at the content width token; step title, one line of help, the control, then actions. Spacing `--atlas-spacing-6` between those blocks and `--atlas-spacing-4` between fields.
- Checklist: a single Card in the main column of the home screen, rows separated by the border token, not nested Cards.

## Hierarchy and composition
- Step title is a question the user can answer ("How will you use the product?"), help text states why it is asked.
- Progress sits above the title. Primary action last; Back and Skip on the same row as ghost.
- The checklist leads with the task that gives value fastest, not a settings task.

## Responsive behavior
- Phone: single column, actions pinned below the control, cards stack. Checklist rows keep the action visible; do not hide it in a menu.

## States
- default · selected (card with checked state) · invalid · loading (Continue `loading`) · skipped · complete.
- empty: a step with no choice keeps Continue enabled only where an answer is required; otherwise offers Skip.
- error: save failure in one Alert; answers stay.

## Accessibility
- The group of cards is a named radio group (`aria-label`). Progress has an accessible label and value text.
- Focus moves to the new step's title on Continue and Back. Checked rows are announced as completed, not only struck through.
- Do not auto-advance on selection.

## Anti-patterns
- A long wizard that asks for everything before showing the product.
- A modal tour that cannot be dismissed.
- Progress with no label, or a checklist with no way to hide it.
- Asking for the same data the user already gave at signup.

## Example
```tsx
import * as React from "react"
import { Alert } from "@atlas/ui-web/compositions/Alert/Alert"
import { Card, CardContent, CardHeader, CardTitle } from "@atlas/ui-web/compositions/Card/Card"
import { ListItem, ListItemActions, ListItemContent, ListItemDescription, ListItemTitle } from "@atlas/ui-web/compositions/ListItem/ListItem"
import { Button } from "@atlas/ui-web/primitives/Button/Button"
import { Input } from "@atlas/ui-web/primitives/Input/Input"
import { Label } from "@atlas/ui-web/primitives/Label/Label"
import { Progress } from "@atlas/ui-web/primitives/Progress/Progress"
import { RadioGroup, RadioGroupItem } from "@atlas/ui-web/primitives/RadioGroup/RadioGroup"

type Setup = { useCase: string; workspace: string }

export function SetupFlow({ onFinish }: { onFinish: (v: Setup) => Promise<void> }) {
  const [step, setStep] = React.useState(0)
  const [useCase, setUseCase] = React.useState("")
  const [workspace, setWorkspace] = React.useState("")
  const [saving, setSaving] = React.useState(false)
  const [failed, setFailed] = React.useState(false)
  const total = 2

  async function next() {
    if (step < total - 1) return setStep(step + 1)
    setSaving(true)
    setFailed(false)
    try {
      await onFinish({ useCase, workspace })
    } catch {
      setFailed(true)
    } finally {
      setSaving(false)
    }
  }

  return (
    <div style={{ display: "grid", gap: "var(--atlas-spacing-6)" }}>
      <Progress value={step + 1} max={total} label="Setup" valueLabel={`Step ${step + 1} of ${total}`} />
      {step === 0 ? (
        <div style={{ display: "grid", gap: "var(--atlas-spacing-4)" }}>
          <h1>How will you use the product?</h1>
          <p style={{ color: "var(--atlas-foreground-muted)" }}>We use this to set up your first screen.</p>
          <RadioGroup variant="card" aria-label="How you will use the product" value={useCase} onValueChange={setUseCase}>
            <RadioGroupItem value="team" label="For my team" description="Share docs and projects" />
            <RadioGroupItem value="personal" label="For personal use" description="Notes and tasks for you" />
            <RadioGroupItem value="school" label="For school" description="Coursework and research" />
          </RadioGroup>
        </div>
      ) : (
        <div style={{ display: "grid", gap: "var(--atlas-spacing-4)" }}>
          <h1>Name your workspace</h1>
          <div>
            <Label htmlFor="workspace" required>Workspace name</Label>
            <Input id="workspace" value={workspace} onChange={(e) => setWorkspace(e.target.value)} />
          </div>
        </div>
      )}
      {failed && <Alert variant="danger" title="We couldn't save your setup" description="Your answers are still here. Try again." />}
      <div style={{ display: "flex", gap: "var(--atlas-spacing-3)", justifyContent: "space-between" }}>
        {step > 0 ? <Button variant="ghost" onClick={() => setStep(step - 1)}>Back</Button> : <span />}
        <Button variant="primary" loading={saving} disabled={step === 0 ? !useCase : !workspace.trim()} onClick={next}>
          {step === total - 1 ? "Finish" : "Continue"}
        </Button>
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}

type Task = { id: string; title: string; why: string; done: boolean; onStart: () => void }

export function GetStartedChecklist({ tasks, onDismiss }: { tasks: Task[]; onDismiss: () => void }) {
  const done = tasks.filter((t) => t.done).length
  return (
    <Card variant="outlined">
      <CardHeader action={<Button variant="ghost" size="sm" onClick={onDismiss}>Hide</Button>}>
        <CardTitle>Get started</CardTitle>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent>
        <Progress value={done} max={tasks.length} label="Setup progress" valueLabel={`${done} of ${tasks.length} complete`} />
        <ul style={{ display: "grid", gap: "var(--atlas-spacing-2)", listStyle: "none", padding: 0 }}>
          {tasks.map((t) => (
            <ListItem key={t.id} as="li" variant="outline">
              <ListItemContent>
                <ListItemTitle style={t.done ? { textDecoration: "line-through" } : undefined}>{t.title}</ListItemTitle>
                <ListItemDescription>{t.why}</ListItemDescription>
              </ListItemContent>
              <ListItemActions>
                {t.done ? <span>Done</span> : <Button variant="ghost" size="sm" onClick={t.onStart}>Start</Button>}
              </ListItemActions>
            </ListItem>
          ))}
        </ul>
      </CardContent>
    </Card>
  )
}
```
